what: NatWest Group is a large British bank. It serves households and small businesses through NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland and Coutts, and lends to UK corporates. The British government sold the last of its stake in 2025.
customers: UK households, small and medium businesses, large corporates and wealth management clients.
money: current accounts, mortgages and consumer lending
business lending, transaction banking and markets
moat: A current account base that rarely moves, which provides cheap deposits, and one of the largest shares of UK business banking.
risks: UK mortgage competition has squeezed lending margins
A weak UK economy raises loan losses
Bank taxes and levies in the UK are high
Deposit costs rise as customers move money to savings accounts
opportunities: The end of government ownership removes an overhang on the shares
Hedging of its deposit book keeps lifting interest income as old positions roll
A dividend yield above 6% plus buybacks returns most of its earnings
watch: Net interest margin and the impairment charge on loans.
